content.text:
Nanjing has four main international schools for families with foreign passports. Several well-known bilingual private schools also teach mostly Chinese-passport students.

**For foreign passport holders**

A 2026 guide for families names the main choices as
Nanjing International School (full IB, non-profit), The British School of Nanjing (English National Curriculum to A level), EtonHouse in Jianye and BASIS in Xianlin.

1. **Nanjing International School (NIS)**, in Xianlin, Qixia District
   - It is the oldest and best known.
It was founded in 1992 by three expatriate families and describes itself as the first IB Continuum school in China.
It is accredited by the International Baccalaureate for all three programmes (PYP, MYP, DP), which cover primary through high school.
It is also accredited by the Council of International Schools (CIS) and the Western Association of Schools and Colleges (WASC).
- Fees:
annual fees for 2025–2026 run from RMB 252,716 at the primary level to RMB 268,956 for Grades 11–12.
- Best for:
families who want the full IB from age 3 and a broad international mix.

2. **The British School of Nanjing (BSN)**, in Jiangning District
   - It is part of Nord Anglia, and
it is the longest-running British international school in Nanjing.
It opened in August 2007 for the children of expatriate families and now teaches ages 2 to 18.
Its students come from about 40 nationalities.
It's about a 30-minute drive south of the city centre (Xinjiekou)
, and
it runs 10 bus routes.
- Best for:
British and Commonwealth families and anyone heading to UK universities.

3. **EtonHouse International School**, in Jianye District
   -
It teaches an international curriculum in English for children aged 2 to 13.
Fees

4. **BASIS International School Nanjing**, in Xianlin

**Other well-regarded schools, mostly bilingual or for Chinese nationals**

These include
Wycombe Abbey School Nanjing, HT Schools Nanjing and Royal Grammar School Guildford, Nanjing

. There are also international departments at top local high schools, such as Nanjing Foreign Language School and Jinling High School.

**Things to know before choosing**
- **Your passport decides which schools you can use.** National rules say these schools
shall enrol the children of foreign personnel holding residence certificates in China and shall not enrol the children of Chinese citizens

. Expat families can use the four schools above. Families with Chinese passports usually look at Wycombe Abbey, RGS Guildford or the local international departments.
- **Location matters.** NIS and BASIS are in the northeast (Xianlin), BSN is in the south (Jiangning), and EtonHouse is central (Jianye). Commute times can be long, so many families pick housing near the school.

**Bottom line:** For a K–12 international education, NIS (IB) and BSN (British) are generally seen as the top two. Choose based on which curriculum you want and where you plan to live. Fees change every year, so check current fees and visit the campuses before deciding.
